audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called every stage 'Skill' with generic template whys and male pronouns, hiding a lane that genuinely swings.
audit.why: Anivia is female. Early she is immobile, Flash Frost costs 80 mana at rank 1 and reaches 1075 while Frostbite only reaches 650 — Lux pokes for free. From 6 the Rebirth egg plus Glacial Storm ends the kill pressure.
audit.corrected: Early stages go to Lux, from level 6 to Anivia, with whys naming the real ranges and the egg. Pronouns corrected throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer sides read 'Skill' while content win[0-3]='Lux' and win[4-6]='Anivia' — the page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways on every row.
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the content layer, and the content prose (spikes, early/mid/late) describes exactly that swing. The full layer's flat 'Skill' column was the stale half.
audit.corrected: phases[0-3].side to Lux, phases[4-6].side to Anivia, matching win[] already on disk, with ratings and whys rewritten in the same group. Spikes: Lux's pre-mana poke window, level 6 Glacial Storm and egg, Anivia's mana-item stabilisation, late zone control.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Flash Frost into Frostbite doubling was described vaguely and no cooldown was anywhere in the cooldown field; the packet flags zero sequencing advice in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot's E text doubles damage if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost or a fully formed Glacial Storm. Q is 11s at rank 1, E is 4s, Crystallize is 17s, and Glacial Storm is a channel she pays mana for each second.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now sequences it: sidestep the 11s Q and the 4s Frostbite is only chip; Crystallize's 17s wall cuts escape, not poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now explains the Illumination auto weave against her 11s Q; dontsFull[2].d explains Final Spark's 60s against Glacial Storm objective fights.

edits.after: Q-poking on cooldown, then walking into a Flash Frost stun with no root banked — that chain is where her Frostbite doubles.

edits.before: - Anivia Flash Frost (Stun): matchup-defining — The slow-moving stun starts every Anivia kill — sidestep it and her E never doubles. It governs your forward steps. - W Prismatic Barrier spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Flash Frost (Q): 11s at rank 1 over 1075 range — the slow orb starts every kill and is what makes Frostbite double, so sidestep it and her 4s E is only chip. - Crystallize is a 17s wall: it cuts your escape, not your poke. - Glacial Storm bleeds her mana every second she holds it.
